clue.text: Sage I'd omitted separately from formal food item, stuffing weighed

indicators.note: stuffing means filling the inside of something else, so the shortened word goes into the next one
the two named letters are dropped, each from its own place in the word for food, not as a pair

parts.note: first part of SAT, weighed in the sense of pressed down upon
VIAND, a formal word for an article of food, minus its I and D
last letter of SAT, closing round the stuffing
the letters I and D, to be removed

explanation.surface: A wise person, keeping their distance, declines a fancy dish that a heavy diner has filled up on.
explanation.walkthrough: VIAND loses its I and its D from separate places, leaving VAN, which goes inside SAT (weighed, as a load sits on something) to make SAVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned scholar, so it is a close synonym for a sage.

clue.text: Tenor interrupting part of his programme once annoyed

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one letter is set inside another word

parts.note: a singer's programme is made up of songs
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A tenor breaks into a colleague's recital, and the colleague is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the answer as an obsolete form, so expect an old past tense rather than a modern word.
explanation.definitionFit: STONG is an old past tense of sting, and to be stung is to be irritated or vexed.

clue.text: Some change in Iceland, air beginning to resonate

parts.note: an aura is an air or atmosphere about a person or place

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Coins jingling in an Icelandic pocket while the air starts to ring with sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurar are small Icelandic coins, plural of eyrir, a hundredth of a krona, so they are loose change there.

clue.text: Cowardly fellow of yore opposed to Trojan, old

parts.note: V for versus, against
Iliac means of Ilium, that is of Troy
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old coward from history who took sides against the Trojans.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium was the Latin name for Troy, so ILIAC can mean Trojan.
explanation.definitionFit: Viliaco is an obsolete Elizabethan word, from Italian, for a villain or coward, hence a craven fellow of the past.

clue.text: Note a stem enclosing upright vowel in foreign script

indicators.note: to enclose is to surround, so the vowel sits inside the plant word

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note
taken as written
a stalk is a plant stem
the vowel I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: A musical note on a stem, with a vowel standing upright, as written in some exotic script.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside STALK as STAL-I-K, after N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastalik (nastaliq) is the flowing Perso-Arabic calligraphic hand used for Persian and Urdu, a script of a foreign language.

clue.text: Tottie in a san suffering process involving muscle spasms

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Tottie, laid up in a sanatorium, is going through a convulsive ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A san is a sanatorium, a hospital for long-term patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanisation is the production of tetanus, a sustained contraction of a muscle from rapidly repeated stimuli.

clue.text: More than one cutting left-overs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: several newspaper cuttings, as pasted into a scrapbook
second meaning: remnants of food after a meal

explanation.surface: Several sharp remarks about leftover food, or a clipping of something left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both clippings collected from print and the uneaten remains of a meal.

clue.text: He deserves death penalty, to wit something that facilitates hanging permits

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
a peg is something to hang a coat on
to allow is to permit

explanation.surface: A man who merits execution, the hanging made easy by permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' points at the gallows, but the hanging here is of clothes on a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegallows is an old word for a rogue who has escaped, or deserves, the hangman's noose.

clue.text: Cross that's crudely fashioned by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says a word is to be heard rather than seen, so the spelling changes but the sound does not

parts.note: rude here means rough or primitively made

explanation.surface: A cross that has been roughly hacked together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a cross or crucifix, especially one set over a church's chancel screen.

clue.text: It helps to stimulate growth that all can view when fed to cuttin'

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: axing, with the dropped G the apostrophe signals
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A plant hormone, safe for everyone to see, that is given to cuttings to make them root.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes after A in AXIN. The apostrophe in cuttin' tells the solver to drop the final G from the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: Auxin is a plant hormone that promotes cell elongation, which is why it is used in rooting powders.

clue.text: Given to sermons a church introduced to quarry

taken as written

last letter of PREY

clue.text: Outings such as bell-ringers are familiar with?

definitions.text: such as bell-ringers are familiar with
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the woolly grips on a bell rope that ringers hold

explanation.walkthrough: In bell-ringing, the sally is the soft striped grip woven into the rope; the question mark flags the specialist sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both trips out or sudden sorties and the padded hand-grips on church bell ropes.

clue.text: Large fish I netted — it involves vigorous hand movements (5, 1 or 2 words)

parts.note: first part of TUNA, a large sea fish
taken as written
rest of TUNA

explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TUNA. The count shows it may also be written TUI NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuina is a Chinese therapeutic massage using brisk pushing and kneading with the hands.

clue.text: Pigeon or duck in pie involving ragu

parts.note: the letters to be mixed
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.walkthrough: In printing, pie is type spilled into a muddle. A ragu is an Italian meat sauce.

clue.text: It helps in fighting the flab — enrol in varying rota

parts.note: first two letters of a rearrangement of the word

clue.text: Measure ring behind second of stirrups

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tape measure

explanation.walkthrough: The stapes is the stirrup-shaped bone of the middle ear; its adjective is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stapedial means relating to the stapes, the stirrup bone, so it is 'of stirrups' in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: E.g dal creating trouble for Indian village

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pulse such as chickpea, from which dal is made
second meaning: an obsolete word for grief or vexation
third meaning: the Hindi word for a village

explanation.surface: A lentil dish stirs up a fuss in a village in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: 'creating' and 'for' just join them, which reads oddly, as the Fifteensquared blog noted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a pulse, an old term for sorrow or anger, and the Indian word for a village, as in gram panchayat.

clue.text: Disputed trio on place for orchestra?

parts.note: a trio is three
the orchestra pit in a theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only puts one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Threepit is the Scots past tense of threep, to argue or insist stubbornly, so it means contended.

clue.text: Partners for eyes trouncing rings

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Unci is the plural of uncus, a hook, and hooks pair with eyes as dress fastenings.

clue.text: Support, easy to carry, part of photographer's armoury?

parts.note: to back is to support
something light is easy to carry

explanation.surface: A lightweight portable stand for a camera kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlight is a lamp placed behind the subject, one of the tools a photographer uses.

clue.text: Pomposity

this is the competition word: solvers were invited to write their own clue for it

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's competition puzzle, so this entry was printed with a bare definition and no wordplay; there is nothing cryptic to unpick here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is inflated, high-sounding language, the verbal form of self-important pomposity.

clue.text: Sunken passage round US building, 100 sq m off

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area equal to 100 square metres
off as in away, absent

explanation.surface: An American basement passage, set off a short distance from the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage an areaway is a sunken court or passage giving light and access to a basement.

clue.text: Tailed car I abandoned nabbed by a tec in disguise

parts.note: first letter of the rearranged letters

clue.text: A dry sari's crumpled and gets out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Line given to one 'of infinite jest' not OK in song?

clue.text: Unknown place for learning Pueblo language

clue.text: Part of guitar concerto no longer plucked

the letters rearranged
last letter of BIT

clue.text: Somewhat faint? Allergic condition may be controlled by it
